heading: Compare rental-service vendors by scope, coverage, and response
body:
A vendor listing identifies a business to investigate. It does not establish that the provider has accepted your property, offers vacation-rental turnover service, or has a partnership with the directory. Confirm scope and coverage directly before building the operating plan around a provider.

Ask the same questions of every candidate

Give each provider the property location, access constraints, expected service, turnover window, and communication needs. Ask what is included, what costs extra, who performs the work, and how completion is documented. A quote for standard residential cleaning may not include linen management, replenishment, inspection photographs, or same-day turnover.

For a fictional cleaning comparison, a $160 quote including laundry and restocking may cover different work from a $130 quote excluding both. Put the missing services and their costs beside the quoted price before ranking providers. Ask whether the provider has capacity during your busiest days, not merely whether the company serves the general market.

Plan the exception before it happens

Confirm how late checkout, unexpected damage, missing supplies, and access failures are handled. Identify who can approve extra work, how urgent issues are escalated, and what happens if the scheduled provider is unavailable. Verify licenses, insurance, references, and other qualifications where relevant to the work and jurisdiction.

Keep a primary provider and a realistic backup plan. A backup contact is useful only when availability, property access, and scope have been discussed. Directory contact details are a research starting point; service acceptance, prices, and operating commitments should be confirmed directly and recorded in your own vendor file.
